chemicals.concentration_notes: or potency: In small, controlled amounts, salt is an essential nutrient required for a cat's body to properly regulate hydration and electrolytes4. Toxicity is heavily dependent on water consumption; it occurs when a cat ingests an excessive amount of salt without having continuous access to fresh drinking water to balance it out.
chemicals.description: Ingesting excessive salt leads to a condition known as salt toxicosis, hypernatremia, or sodium ion poisoning1. As the concentration of sodium in the blood serum increases, it creates a powerful osmotic gradient that rapidly draws water out of the body's cells (the intracellular and interstitial compartments) and into the extracellular fluid.
chemicals.name: Sodium Chloride (Sodium Ion)

description:
While a small amount of sodium is essential for a cat's health, too much salt is toxic. A large ingestion of salt can lead to a dangerous condition known as salt poisoning or hypernatremia. This happens when high levels of sodium build up in the blood.

The excess sodium in the bloodstream pulls water out of the body's cells in an attempt to balance itself. This process causes cells to shrivel and can lead to severe dehydration, especially damaging the brain and nervous system. The risk is highest when a cat consumes a lot of salt without access to plenty of fresh water to flush it out.

Common sources of salt poisoning are human foods like potato chips, cured meats, or homemade play-dough. Symptoms include extreme thirst, vomiting, diarrhea, weakness, stumbling, and seizures. Salt poisoning is a medical emergency that requires immediate veterinary intervention.
emergencyNote: If a cat ingests a toxic amount of salt
name: Salt
safetyNotes: Toxic dose: approximately 4g/kg body weight is lethal; smaller amounts cause significant symptoms; even salty snacks fed regularly cause cumulative harm
Mechanism: high serum sodium causes cell dehydration and cerebral oedema; severe disruption of neurological and cardiac function
Symptoms: excessive thirst, frequent urination, vomiting, diarrhea, weakness, tremors, seizures; severe cases cause kidney failure and death
Salty human foods (chips, cured meats, soy sauce) are the most common accidental exposure route
If your cat ingests a large amount of salt or salty food, contact your vet immediately

symptoms.name: If a cat ingests or is exposed to excessive amounts of salt without adequate access to fresh water
Severe Gastrointestinal Upset
symptoms.notes: The influx of excessive salt causes direct osmotic irritation and inflammation of the gastrointestinal mucosa, triggering vomiting and diarrhea.
symptoms.onset: Within minutes to a few hours of ingestion

symptoms.name: Excessive Thirst and Urination
symptoms.notes: The extreme thirst is the cat's biological attempt to restore osmotic balance4. The excess sodium circulating in the blood draws fluid out of the body's cells, leading to severe cellular dehydration, which the body frantically tries to correct by seeking water.

symptoms.name: Neurological Deficits and Brain Damage
symptoms.notes: The brain is uniquely vulnerable to rapid hypernatremia. As the sodium pulls water out of the brain's cells, it causes cerebral dehydration and physical cell shrinkage.
symptoms.onset: Progressive (develops within minutes to hours as the sodium alters cell osmolarity)

symptoms.name: Cardiovascular and Respiratory Distress
symptoms.notes: These symptoms are often accompanied by an elevated body temperature and are secondary to the massive fluid shifts, electrolyte derangements, and systemic shock the body is experiencing.

symptoms.name: Acute Kidney Failure
symptoms.notes: The severe, rapid systemic dehydration caused by the sodium drawing fluid out of the cells can overwhelm and destroy the kidneys, leading to acute kidney failure and death.
symptoms.onset: Progressive (hours to days as the toxicosis advances)

treatments.name: If a cat ingests a toxic amount of salt

treatments.description: of the procedure: If the cat arrives at the clinic already experiencing severe neurological distress, the veterinarian will administer seizure-control agents (such as diazepam) to stop the convulsions. If severe brain swelling (cerebral edema) is suspected, medications like mannitol, dexamethasone, or dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) may be administered to help reduce the pressure in the brain.
treatments.name: Emergency Neurological Stabilization (Seizure Control)
treatments.notes: This takes absolute priority if the cat is actively having seizures or is in a coma, as the severe cellular dehydration caused by hypernatremia directly damages the brain and can cause intracranial hemorrhage.

treatments.description: of the procedure: For mild cases, or if the cat was caught ingesting salt before severe clinical signs have started, the offending food or salt source is immediately removed. The cat is then offered fresh water, but strictly in small amounts at frequent intervals while being closely observed.
treatments.name: Immediate Source Removal and Controlled Oral Hydration
treatments.notes: It is highly dangerous to let a salt-poisoned cat drink a massive amount of pure water all at once. A sudden influx of fresh water can cause fluid to rapidly build up in the brain, drastically worsening neurological signs and causing fatal brain swelling.

treatments.description: of the procedure: The cat is hospitalized, and blood serum sodium levels are closely monitored. The veterinarian administers specific IV fluids (sometimes slightly hypertonic fluids) to correct the cat's free water deficit, dilute the sodium in the blood, and restore electrolyte balance over a period of 2 to 3 days.
treatments.name: Judicious Intravenous (IV) Fluid Therapy and Electrolyte Monitoring
treatments.notes: This is the most complex and critical part of treating salt toxicosis. To survive the extreme salt levels, the cat's brain cells produce "idiogenic osmoles" to maintain their volume.

treatments.description: of the procedure: The veterinarian may administer antacids and/or antibiotics to alleviate the severe gastrointestinal irritation and inflammation caused by the heavy influx of salt.
treatments.name: Symptomatic Gastrointestinal Support
treatments.notes: This is used as an adjunctive treatment to help manage the vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal distress that frequently accompany an acute salt poisoning episode.
